f: Step 1: b_k = 2 x 65 / (31 pi). Step 2: = 1.3348 (4 decimal places). Check: coefficients fall as 1/k, slower than a triangle wave (1/k^2) but faster than the constant spectrum of an impulse train.

q: A DFT uses N = 8192 samples taken at fs = 991232 Hz. The bin spacing is: (spaced-repetition variant 7574)
h: Spacing = fs / N.
f: Step 1: spacing = 991232 / 8192. Step 2: = 121 Hz between bins X[k] and X[k+1]. Check: N bins x 121 Hz spans the full 991232 Hz sampling rate.

q: Output power is 60.71 times the input power. The gain in decibels is:
h: dB = 10 log10(P2/P1) for powers (20 log10 is for voltages).
f: Step 1: ratio = 60.71. Step 2: 10 log10(60.71) = 17.83 dB. Check: ratio 0.5 gives about -3 dB and ratio 10 gives +10 dB; sign follows gain versus loss.

q: A 16-ary modulation runs at 327 baud. Its bit rate is:
h: Bit rate = baud x log2(L).
f: Step 1: bits per symbol = log2(16) = 4. Step 2: bit rate = 327 x 4 = 1308 bps. Check: denser constellations raise rate at fixed baud but need higher SNR for the same error rate.

q: For A = [[0, 1], [-407, -403]] (companion form), det(A) is:
h: det [[p, q],[r, s]] = p s - q r.
f: Step 1: det = (0)(-403) - (1)(-407). Step 2: = 407. Check: det(A) equals the product of eigenvalues, here the constant term of s^2 + 403 s + 407.

q: For x(t) = 969 cos(2 pi 17 t) (1 ohm reference), the average power P is:
h: P = A^2 / 2 for any sinusoid, independent of frequency.
f: Step 1: identify amplitude A = 969. Step 2: P = A^2/2 = 938961/2 = 469480.5. Check: average of cos^2 over a period is 1/2, and frequency 17 Hz does not change the average.

q: Evaluate the integral over all t of (t^2 + 236) delta(t - (326)) dt:
h: Sifting: the impulse samples the bracket at t = t0.
f: Step 1: sifting property: integral of x(t) delta(t - t0) dt = x(t0). Step 2: x(326) = 326^2 + 236 = 106512. Check: everything away from t = 326 is multiplied by zero.

q: The system y[n] = x[n] + x[n - 499] is classified as: (spaced-repetition variant 7575)
o: Memoryless and causal
With memory and noncausal
Memoryless and noncausal
With memory, causal, linear and time-invariant
h: It uses the present sample and a past sample only.
f: Step 1: x[n - 499] is a past sample, so the system has memory. Step 2: no future samples appear, so it is causal. Step 3: it is a fixed linear combination with constant coefficients, hence linear and time-invariant.

q: Convolving x[n] = {719, 128} with h[n] = {624, 662} (both starting at n = 0), the value y[1] is:
X(s) = 1 / ((s + 233)(s + 274)) with causal ROC. In x(t), the coefficient multiplying e^(-233 t) is:
h: Cover-up: set s = -a in 1/(s + b).
f: Step 1: partial fractions: A/(s+233) + B/(s+274) with A = 1/(274 - 233) = 0.0244. Step 2: x(t) = (0.0244 e^(-233 t) - 0.0244 e^(-274 t)) u(t). Check: x(0+) = 0, matching the initial-value behaviour of this strictly proper X(s).

q: x[n] = (0.4569)^n u[n]. The sample x[3] is:
h: Cube the base; u[3] = 1.
f: Step 1: x[3] = (0.4569)^3. Step 2: = 0.0954. Check: |a| = 0.4569 is below 1, so the ROC |z| above 0.4569 includes the unit circle: decaying and stable.
